title: Cao et al. (2024) tectonic and plate boundary evolution over 1.8 billion years
citation: Cao, X., Collins, A. S., Pisarevsky, S., Flament, N., Li, S., Hasterok, D., and Müller, R. D., 2024. Earth's tectonic and plate boundary evolution over 1.8 billion years. Geoscience Frontiers, 15(2), 101922.

relationship: Built by joining two Proterozoic models, P14 (Pisarevsky et al. 2014) for 1770-1270 Ma and C21 (Condie et al. 2021) elsewhere in 1800-1100 Ma, onto the Phanerozoic line this project already carries. Measured against merdith2021, 96% of their shared rotation sequences are byte-identical and 50 sequences are new, so inside the 0-650 Ma window this viewer shows the two reconstructions nearly coincide. What this model adds is reach: it is the only one here that goes past 1 Ga.
limitations: Longitude in the Precambrian rests on palaeomagnetism alone and is weakly constrained. The deep-time half comes from different source models than the Phanerozoic half, so the two are not one continuous reconstruction.
viewer_note: The timeline stops at 650 Ma because that is the oldest Scotese map, so the part of this model that is genuinely its own is not reachable yet.
